pr_title: Added optional parameters to QSTR ES|QL function
pr_body:
Adds options to QSTR function.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/118619 added named function parameters. This PR uses this mechanism for allowing query string function parameters, so [query string parameters](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-query-string-query.html#query-string-top-level-params) can be used in ES|QL.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/120933

issue_context.title: ESQL - Add options to QSTR function
issue_context.body:
### Description

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/120360/ added options to MATCH function. We want to add options to the QSTR function as well.

Steps for doing this would be:

## Modify `QueryStringQuery` in ESQL
 - Reference the fields used in the query builder instead of creating new constants, like here.
 - Change the constructor so options are passed in as a `Map<String, Object>`

## Modify QueryString function to implement options:
  - Make it implement `OptionalArgument` as a marker for adding a new optional param
  - Get the supported [options](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-query-string-query.html#query-string-top-level-params) from query string query (similar to [this](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d91d51600e0e35e24087f6fcf793ec0efd8907d5/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L127))
  - Add them to the documentation in the form of `@MapParam` annotation (like [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d91d51600e0e35e24087f6fcf793ec0efd8907d5/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L176))
  - Add constructors to provide options as an additional expression ([here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d91d51600e0e35e24087f6fcf793ec0efd8907d5/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L262))
  - We'll need to resolve the types for the provided options to ensure that they are valid. [This](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d91d51600e0e35e24087f6fcf793ec0efd8907d5/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L341) is the work done in match - we probably want some utility class or method on a superclass to deal with common code here.
  - We'll need to [create a Map](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/120360/files#diff-2a2a93511cb0302ea16f221502140421c53428ac84a620dbe4601def14414a49R362) with the options to provide them to the `QueryStringQuery` in the [translate()](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d91d51600e0e35e24087f6fcf793ec0efd8907d5/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/fulltext/Match.java#L362) method.

## Add tests
- Add tests to `AnalyzerTests` (similar to [this](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcd8d159d68fa13baf7c394cdeac0db7543d1fa4/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/AnalyzerTests.java#L2590) ) to ensure the analysis is done properly and options are included in the query builder.
- Add tests to `VerifierTests` (similar to [these](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcd8d159d68fa13baf7c394cdeac0db7543d1fa4/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/VerifierTests.java#L2005)) to ensure verification is done for the option types, and they work as expected.
- Add tests to `QueryStringTests` so we test all the combinations for the types, similar to [this](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/120360/files#diff-40fa599760baac356f435ae0b05e1e54e57fcb4637bdcbd6194c1eec4d6eb505R48). Tests that extend from `AbstractFunctionTestCase` also generates docs under /docs/reference/esql/functions based on the constructor annotations and the types that are used as test cases in the corresponding function test.
- Add tests to `LocalPhysicalPlanOptimizerTests` to ensure options are translated into the actual query when it gets pushed down to Lucene (see [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/60935e82c1b78115302876dfe9420e90b79c3df7/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/optimizer/LocalPhysicalPlanOptimizerTests.java#L1584)). 

## Add docs
- Docs should be generated automatically from the constructor annotations. Check that we are referencing the `<<esql-function-named-params,function named parameters>>` so users can look at details on how to pass function named params.
- If you change the doc annotations, run `QueryStringTests` to re-generate them.

review_comments: This is essentially the same as the Match options one, not sure if it is worth refactoring....

Yes, I think it would be good to have common code for `match` and `qstr` options.

We can include it in `FullTextFunctions`, or have a separate utility class.

I looked into this, but it does not produce a good interface. There are a lot of options needed to be passed to this utility class which IMO defeats the purpose. Lets keep separate, which would allow both to evolve and be fixed independently if needed. Same for the testing change below.
That's ok, we can do that as a follow up PR if needed be.
We can probably extract this testing code to a separate method so both `match` and `qstr` can reuse it
It would be a good idea to add the default values for each field, so users understand what is expected if they don't provide it. This is something we need to do in MATCH.
I was wondering about how to do that. Are there are examples you can point me to?

I mean adding the default values in the `description`, so we would have something like:

```
name = "analyze_wildcard",
                    type = "keyword",
                    valueHint = { "false" },
                    description = "If true, the query attempts to analyze wildcard terms in the query string. Defaults to false."
```

The "defaults to false" bit is what we can add to the options description so users are aware of the default values, and don't have to go looking at the query string docs for it.
I see... I have defaults for some descriptions but not others. Will make another pass.
